why: I checked all three must_catch items, and the briefs handle each one. (1) Builder step 2 says to "add a section for slugify (e.g. "## slugify(s)" ...) and a section for padLeft". Its context also says README has "NO section for slugify". (2) Verifier Check 3 lists the exports and says "at the head this should include capitalize, slugify, truncate and padLeft". Its FAIL condition is "any exported function has no section in README.md (note: slugify had no section before this change, so check it specifically)". (3) Check 1 calls `m.padLeft('ab', 5)` with no fill argument and requires the result to be '   ab', so it checks space padding. One side note: in Check 3's command, the shell turns `'\\b'` into `'\b'`, which JS reads as a backspace character. That could make the command report a false FAIL. It doesn't stop the brief from catching the trap: the FAIL criteria are right, and the verifier is also told to open README.md and look.
